Newly appointed CEO John Ternus is planning a "comprehensive overhaul" of Apple, aiming to make the company "operate faster and more leanly", according to the latest report from Bloomberg. The reforms include a series of measures such as launching more products and cutting "middle management positions".

John Ternus hopes to reshape Apple — here are his reform directives

First, the new Apple CEO wants to roll out more products at a faster pace than before, including becoming "more boldly experimental". One idea is to break away from Apple's traditional spring and autumn launch rhythm, and instead spread new product launches throughout the year.

Ternus also hopes to "build a more streamlined organisation more focused on engineering R&D", which involves a number of cost-cutting and restructuring measures. For example, one of the changes is to "streamline some middle management positions in order to reduce the layers between engineers and senior management".

The report pointed out that Apple has laid off "a group of engineering project managers (EPMs)" from its hardware engineering department in the past two weeks. Bloomberg described these positions as having "for decades been central to Apple's product development process", responsible for "managing schedules and coordinating work between teams".

The report quoted: "Those affected include a number of project managers, among them around six directors, which is one of the most senior levels of employees at the company. These staff have only been given a few weeks to find other positions within the company; those who fail to transfer will be laid off later this year."

However, Bloomberg said the relevant cost-cutting measures could be rolled out more broadly. Ternus has reportedly argued for years that Apple should become "leaner":

In addition, Apple reportedly shelved a plan this summer to cut 5,000 AppleCare staff, believing that AI agents could handle the relevant work.

At the same time, Ternus hopes to work with Eddy Cue and CFO Kevan Parekh to boost Apple's services revenue. The report said: "They have discussed launching new services, as well as finding more revenue from existing products and businesses."
